Root question: Can one long sequential simulation, like a single MCMC chain or a rainfall-runoff model stepped through decades of daily rainfall, be parallelised over time by guessing the whole trajectory and then correcting every step at once with Newton iterations, and does that only work when the system forgets its past? Is compute a major blocker at some level, and could that be fixed with a shit ton of GPU parallelism?

card:question: Can SAE feature coordinates make a transformer's layer-to-layer transition linear enough to compose out of order by repeated squaring, giving parallel-in-time depth [s_pdiag]?
card:hypothesis: If residual-stream layers are near-linear in SAE features, repeated squaring composes the trajectory in O(log T) depth with no forgetting [s_pdiag].
card:sequential_part: None: each per-feature linearity fit is independent of the others, so no answer waits step after step.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Composed out-of-order prediction reconstructs at least 90% of true activations at all 42 layers, so the linear ParaDiag shortcut holds.
card:if_not: Composed prediction falls below 90% reconstruction and decays with depth, so residual nonlinearity breaks out-of-order composition.
card:test_summary: Fit per-layer linear feature transitions (Gemma 2 9B, Gemma Scope SAEs), compose them out of order by repeated squaring, and score against the sequential forward pass; compare with the published adjacent-layer transport R² of 0.95 [s_ato].
card:closest_prior: Prior work (Activation Transport Operators) measured per-feature R² of linear layer-to-layer maps up to a 10-layer leap on a small open model, in under 50 GPU-hours [s_ato].
card:left_open: It did not compose operators out of order over full depth, sweep SAE width, or test time-invariance across contexts on a production-scale model.
card:anchor: SAE encoder-decoder round-trip reproduces released weights to relative error under 1e-5; composition code matches sequential on a synthetic linear system.
card:limits: Holds for open Gemma/LLaMA models and released SAEs, not Claude 3 Sonnet's 34M features; it measures linearity, not a shipped parallel sampler.
